reasons: Section 22.1 as drafted (audit 'at any time without notice' plus remote access to Customer systems) is squarely in the rule's walk-away territory and fails the fallback on frequency, notice and system access, so the deviation classification is correct.

The redline reaches the preferred position with the necessary scope: once per twelve months, thirty days' prior written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality at least as protective as Section 16, and express removal of system access. The high changed-character ratio is justified because the original sentence had no salvageable limits.
No double-flagging: cost allocation (22.2) and confidentiality of findings (22.3) already meet the preferred position and were correctly left untouched and noted in the rationale.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position, notes consistency with the existing no-direct-access language in 22.2, and offers the fifteen-day fallback.
